title: Canonical truncations lift bounded derived modules to finite filtered localization
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $D^b(R)$ be the full subcategory of $D(R)$ consisting of objects with bounded cohomology [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal D_f(R)=\mathcal H_f(R)[W^{-1}]$ be the localization of uniformly finite filtered module complexes modulo filtration-preserving homotopies at graded quasi-isomorphisms [def-kun-finite-filtered-module-homotopy]. The forgetful and graded functors take values in $D(R)$. Use the standard good truncations [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]: $\tau_{\le m}K$ has the old terms below $m$, $\ker d^m$ in degree $m$ and zero above.
There is a functor $\mathcal T:D^b(R)\to\mathcal D_f(R)$ whose value on a bounded termwise complex $K$ representing $C$ is the class of $(K,F^iK=\tau_{\le-i}K)$, and whose value on a chain map of bounded representatives is the class of that same map preserving these subcomplexes. There are natural isomorphisms of functors
$$\omega\mathcal T\cong\operatorname{incl}:D^b(R)\to D(R),\qquad \operatorname{gr}^i\mathcal T(C)\cong H^{-i}(C)[i].$$
On bounded complexes the graded comparison is induced by the quotient from the two-term complex $\operatorname{im}d^{-i-1}\hookrightarrow\ker d^{-i}$ in degrees $-i-1,-i$ to $H^{-i}(K)$ in degree $-i$. For every derived morphism $u:C\to C'$ its graded morphism under this comparison is $H^{-i}(u)[i]$, and its underlying morphism is $u$. The functor and these comparisons are independent of bounded representatives up to natural isomorphism compatible with the specified representative-level formulas. No termwise functorial choice of a bounded representative is asserted.

Explicit simultaneous-filtration functoriality extension of the source construction.

proof.text: Let $C\in D^b(R)$. By [lem-kun-bounded-derived-roofs], choose a bounded cochain representative $K$ and an isomorphism $Q(K)\cong C$. For a derived morphism $u:C\to C'$, choose bounded representatives $K,L$ and a bounded roof $K\xleftarrow{s}M\xrightarrow{g}L$ for $u$, with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism. Thus all representative-level constructions below may be made with bounded complexes and bounded roofs; no termwise functorial representative is chosen. Form the full subcategory of termwise bounded complexes and its homotopy quotient. The bounded roofs and common-refinement clauses show that the functor from this quotient to the bounded derived category is essentially surjective, every morphism is a right roof, and equality of images of two maps is killed by a quasi-isomorphism. These properties give a right calculus of fractions on this bounded homotopy category and identify its localization with the bounded derived category (Mathlib localization construction and full-faithful criterion).

For a bounded representative $K$, apply [lem-kun-canonical-truncation-filtration]. The subcomplexes $F^iK=\tau_{\le-i}K$ form a finite decreasing filtration, and every chain map preserves them. The quotient in filtration degree $i$ is the two-term complex $\operatorname{im}d^{-i-1}\hookrightarrow\ker d^{-i}$, with its natural quasi-isomorphism to $H^{-i}(K)[i]$. A chain homotopy gives a filtration-preserving homotopy after truncation, so the class of $(K,F)$ is well defined in $\mathcal H_f(R)$ for a bounded homotopy representative.

proof.text: On bounded complexes, send K to its canonical finite filtered complex and a chain map to its unique filtration-preserving lift. The homotopy clause of [lem-kun-canonical-truncation-filtration] makes this descend to the bounded homotopy quotient. Its graded quasi-isomorphism clause sends every quasi-isomorphism to an invertible map in the finite filtered localization [def-kun-finite-filtered-module-homotopy]. Thus the localization universal property established in Step 1 gives the functor T on the bounded derived category and the comparison on every bounded representative. The naturality of the localization comparison gives its chain-map formula; applying that formula to a quasi-isomorphism and then canceling gives the roof formula. No calculus of fractions in the filtered target is required. Obtain the target forgetful and graded functors, their localization lifting isomorphisms, and their representative-map equations from [lem-kun-filtered-tensor-localization].

source.place: Tags 05S2 and 05S6; canonical truncation construction in Tag 0H7Z

proof.text: The forgetful functor $\omega:\mathcal D_f(R)\to D(R)$ sends the filtered roof in Step 3 to the same ordinary roof. On an object represented by $K$, the composite $\omega\mathcal T$ is $Q(K)$, and on a chain-map roof it is the original derived morphism. The bounded-roof independence from Steps 1 and 3 therefore supplies a natural isomorphism $\omega\mathcal T\cong\operatorname{incl}:D^b(R)\to D(R)$ whose component at $C$ is the chosen identification $Q(K)\cong C$.

source.place: Tags 05S2 and 05S6, localization functor and bounded representatives

proof.text: For each i compose the target graded comparison, the image under Q of the natural quasi-isomorphism pi from Step 2, the single-complex shift isomorphism, and the inverse of the canonical homology comparison Q(K). This is a natural isomorphism on bounded complexes: paste the graded comparison naturality, the pi naturality, the shift naturality, and the homology comparison naturality. Descend it first through the homotopy quotient and then through the localization from Step 1 using the fully faithful restriction of natural transformations. Do the same for the forgetful comparison in Step 4. Evaluation on representatives gives exactly the required normalization equations. Naturality along the chosen representative isomorphism proves these equations for every eC; the two final morphism equations are the naturality of these descended isomorphisms. This proves compatibility for all roofs and independence of representatives.
